newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Not all expect rebound to last.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Not all expect rebound to last.

text.p: U.S. stocks continued their rebound on Tuesday, but index options traders said not all investors expected the bounce to last.
By about 1030 CDT/1530 GMT, the bellwether Dow industrial average .DJI was up 83 points at 6,535 after gaining 60 points Monday.
The S&P 500 index .SPX added nearly 8.0 points to 751.44 and the S&P 100 index .OEX rose 7.0 to about 730.
June S&P 500 futures were up 8.40 at 755.70. One firm pegged fair value at 4.92 points over cash, buy programs at 5.60 points over and sell programs at 4.30 points over.
Traders and analysts pegged Tuesday's rally to a better than expected consumer price report for March.
"It's just the way those numbers were interpreted," one major index options trader in Chicago said. "Bonds took off and everything looks rosy again.
"But right now it's a one-day deal," he said. "The market seems to be settled into accepting a 10 percent correction and we're going to have some little bounces along the way."
The Dow industrials reached an all-time closing high of 7,085 on March 11. Ten percent off that would take the Dow to about 6,300.
June S&P 500 futures have already corrected 10 percent off their contract high of 827.80.
Even so, few traders were willing to call an end to the correction, particularly as index put buying remained strong.
"We've had mostly put buyers," one OEX trader in Chicago said. "I don't think a lot of people believe (the bounce)."
By 1030 CDT/1530 GMT, OEX put volume outpaced call volume by 53,623 to 50,801. Among SPX options at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, puts beat calls by 36,843 to 19,417.
But investors' interest in the puts has contrarians expecting further gains.

In a report, Todd Salamone, an analyst at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute, said the CBOE's combined equity and index put-call ratio registered its first bullish reading since mid-December last year on Monday at 0.99.
He added that last Friday, as the market fell sharply, the put-call ratio was a "near bullish" 0.92.
In OEX trading Tuesday, the April 730 put and call were battling for the most active slot. The call had traded about 10,760 contracts by 1050 CDT/1550 GMT and the put had traded about 10,400.

Traders noted that a large number of OEX April in-the-money puts remain open ahead of expiration and that if a large portion of them are exercised, the market could bounce further. But if positions are unwound, the holders would have to sell stock first, which could cut the market's rally short.
Jon Najarian, president of Mercury Trading, said in a report one sign the market remains in correction mode is the reaction to Intel Corp's strong quarterly earnings.
"When Intel has a blowout number and they still manage to take the stock down, that's a sign that we are in a correction phase still," he said. Intel was down 3-1/4 to 130-1/2.
